title: Offerings at the Tabernacle
summary: The LORD speaks from the tent of meeting and sets out the offerings: the burnt offering wholly consumed on the altar, the grain offering, the peace offering shared with the worshiper, and the sin and guilt offerings for unintentional sins and for wrongs against God or a neighbor. Each comes with instructions on the animal, the blood and fat, and the priests' portions. Together they describe how Israelites approach God with sacrifice.

title: Aaron and His Sons Are Ordained
summary: Moses assembles the congregation and washes, clothes and anoints Aaron and his sons, with sin, burnt and ordination offerings; blood is put on their right ear, thumb and toe. They remain at the tent door seven days. On the eighth day Aaron offers the first sacrifices for himself and the people, and he and Moses bless them. The glory of the LORD appears, fire consumes the offering on the altar, and the people shout and fall on their faces.

title: Nadab and Abihu
summary: Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons, offer strange fire that the LORD had not commanded, and fire from the LORD kills them. Moses says the LORD will be sanctified in those near him, and Aaron is silent. Their cousins carry the bodies out of the camp, and Aaron and his remaining sons are forbidden to mourn openly or to drink wine in the tent. Moses is angry over a sin offering that was burned, not eaten, but accepts Aaron's explanation.

title: Clean and Unclean Animals
summary: God sets out which animals Israel may eat: land animals that chew the cud and have divided hooves, water creatures with fins and scales, and certain birds and winged insects. The camel, pig, hare and shellfish are among those forbidden, along with birds of prey and creeping things, and touching their carcasses makes a person unclean until evening. The chapter closes by tying the rules to God's call: be holy, because I am holy.

title: Purity After Childbirth, Skin Disease and Mold
summary: Instructions cover purification after childbirth, with a longer period of uncleanness for a daughter than a son, and the priest's examination of skin disease, with isolation, shaving and rules for infected clothing and houses. A person healed of leprosy is cleansed with two birds, water and oil, and offerings on the eighth day. Chapter 15 sets rules for bodily discharges. The aim in each case is to keep the camp and the tabernacle from defilement.

title: The Day of Atonement
summary: After the death of Aaron's sons, God sets out the Day of Atonement. Once a year Aaron may enter the most holy place, after bathing and putting on linen garments, with incense and the blood of a bull for himself and a goat for the people. Two goats are chosen by lot: one is killed as a sin offering, and the other, after Aaron confesses Israel's sins over its head, is sent into the wilderness. The people are to afflict themselves and do no work.

title: Holiness Laws
summary: The holiness laws cover where sacrifices may be offered, the ban on eating blood, forbidden sexual relations, honest dealing, love of neighbor and of the stranger, penalties for offenses such as offering children to Molech, and the purity and conduct required of priests and their offerings. 'Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy' recurs throughout, and many laws end with 'I am the LORD.'

title: The Appointed Festivals
summary: The LORD sets out the feasts Israel is to keep: the weekly Sabbath, Passover and Unleavened Bread, the offering of firstfruits, Pentecost fifty days later, the blast of trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and Tabernacles, when Israel lives in booths for seven days. Each has its date, offerings and rest from work. The harvest instructions leave the edges of the field for the poor and the stranger.

title: The Blasphemer Stoned
summary: The son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father blasphemes the Name in a quarrel in the camp. He is held until the LORD's will is known, and the LORD tells Moses that those who heard him are to lay hands on his head and the congregation is to stone him. The passage restates that one law applies to the native and the stranger, with penalties matching the injury done, and the sentence is carried out.

title: The Sabbath Year and Jubilee
summary: Every seventh year the land is to rest, with no sowing or reaping, and the LORD promises enough harvest in the sixth. Every fiftieth year, the Jubilee, begins on the Day of Atonement with a trumpet: land returns to its family, and Israelites who sold themselves are freed. Laws provide for redeeming land and relatives and forbid interest on loans to a poor kinsman, since Israelites belong to the LORD and are not to be treated as slaves.

title: Blessings and Curses
summary: God promises rain, harvest, peace and his presence among them if Israel keeps his commands, and warns of escalating punishments for disobedience: disease, defeat, famine, ruin and scattering among the nations. Even then he will remember the covenant with Jacob, Isaac and Abraham if the people confess. The book ends with rules for valuing vows, devoted things and the tithe, and the note that these are the commandments given at Sinai.
